---

## 🚀 Quick Start Guide

### Step 1: Build LamiaComms CLI Client
```cmd
cd C:\LamiaFabrica
build_lamiacomms_cli.bat
```

### Step 2: Store Server Credentials
```cmd
lamiacomms_cli.exe
lamiacomms> vault store vps1 10.0.0.1 root password123 22
lamiacomms> vault store vps2 10.0.0.2 root password123 22
lamiacomms> vault store vps3 10.0.0.3 root password123 22
lamiacomms> vault store vps4 10.0.0.4 root password123 22
```

### Step 3: Deploy to Server
```cmd
lamiacomms> connect vps1
lamiacomms> deploy vps1 fccp_server
lamiacomms> install vps1
lamiacomms> control vps1 start
```

### Step 4: Verify Control
```cmd
lamiacomms> exec vps1 "systemctl status fccp-server"
lamiacomms> exec vps1 "ls -lh /opt/medusaserv/bin/"
```

---

## 📋 Complete Command Reference

### Credential Management:
```cmd
vault store <id> <host> <user> <pass> [port]  - Store credential
vault get <id>                                  - Get credential
vault list                                     - List credentials
```

### Server Control:
```cmd
connect <server_id>                            - Connect to server
exec <server_id> <command>                      - Execute command
deploy <server_id> <file>                       - Deploy file
install <server_id>                            - Install FCCP
control <server_id> <action>                    - Control server
```

### CRUD Operations:
```cmd
create <table> <field=value> ...               - Create record
read <table> [field=value] ...                  - Read records
update <table> <field=value> ... WHERE ...       - Update records
delete <table> WHERE <field=value> ...          - Delete records
```

### File Transfer:
```cmd
upload <local> <remote>                         - Upload file
download <remote> <local>                        - Download file
sync <local_dir> <remote_dir>                    - Sync directories
```

---

## 🔐 Secure Vault Usage

### Storing Credentials:
The Secure Vault uses **AES-256-GCM encryption** with LFSSL native crypto:

```cmd
lamiacomms> vault store vps1 10.0.0.1 root mypassword 22
✅ Credential stored: vps1
```

**Storage Location:**
- Windows: `C:\Users\<username>\AppData\Roaming\LamiaFabrica\vault.enc`
- Encrypted with master key
- Secure credential retrieval

### Automatic Credential Usage:
When you use commands like:
- `connect vps1` - Automatically retrieves credentials from vault
- `exec vps1 "command"` - Uses vault credentials for SSH
- `deploy vps1 file` - Uses vault credentials for connection

---

## 🐧 Ubuntu Installation Process

### What the Installer Does:

1. **Updates System** - Latest packages
2. **Installs Dependencies** - Build tools, libraries
3. **Creates Service User** - `medusaserv` user
4. **Creates Directories** - `/opt/medusaserv/`
5. **Sets Up Socket** - `/var/run/fccp.sock`
6. **Installs Binaries** - FCCP server/client
7. **Creates Systemd Service** - Auto-start on boot
8. **Configures Logging** - Log rotation
9. **Starts Service** - Immediate activation

### Installation Locations:

   ```bash
chmod +x BUILD_INTEGRITY_AGENT.sh
   ```


- ✅ Feature verified and empirically proven

The unified main entry point (`src/psiforcedb_medusaserv_main.cpp`) integrates all features:

# LamiaComms & API Gateway Integration Guide

**Date:** December 18, 2025
**Status:** ✅ INTEGRATION READY

## 🎯 Overview

This document describes the integration between LamiaComms infrastructure management system and the MedusaServ API Gateway, providing a complete infrastructure control and monitoring solution.

## 🏗️ Architecture Integration

### System Components

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│              LamiaComms Infrastructure Layer            │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  ┌──────────────┐  ┌──────────────┐  ┌──────────────┐ │
│  │ TUI Client   │  │ CLI Client   │  │   Server     │ │
│  │ (267 KB)     │  │ (519 KB)     │  │ (220 KB)     │ │
│  └──────┬───────┘  └──────┬───────┘  └──────┬───────┘ │
│         │                  │                  │          │
│         └──────────────────┴──────────────────┘          │
│                          │                               │
│                    LamiaComms Protocol                   │

                           │
                           ▼

│            MedusaServ API Gateway Layer                 │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │
│  │         API Gateway Handler                      │ │
│  │  - Request Routing                              │ │
│  │  - JWT/GUI Token Validation                     │ │
│  │  - Rate Limiting                                │ │
│  └──────────────────┬───────────────────────────────┘ │
│                     │                                  │
│  ┌──────────────────▼───────────────────────────────┐ │
│  │         API Gateway Tree                        │ │
│  │  - Server Discovery                             │ │
│  │  - Health Checks                                │ │
│  │  - Service Registry                             │ │
│  └──────────────────┬───────────────────────────────┘ │
│                     │                                  │
│  ┌──────────────────▼───────────────────────────────┐ │
│  │      Callback System Core                        │ │
│  │  - VPC Routing                                   │ │
│  │  - Circuit Breakers                             │ │
│  │  - Connection Pooling                            │ │
│  └──────────────────┬───────────────────────────────┘ │
└──────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────┘
                       │
                       ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│              Infrastructure Services                    │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  Database Server │ Back Office Server │ Developer Server│
│  (Port 60)       │ (Ports 80/443/666) │ (Port 8080)     │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## 🔗 Integration Points

### 1. Service Discovery Integration

**LamiaComms** can query the **API Gateway Tree** to discover available services:

```cpp
// LamiaComms queries API Gateway for service list
std::string tree_json = api_gateway->getTreeStructure();
// Returns: JSON with all servers and services
```

**Benefits:**
- Automatic service discovery
- Real-time service status
- Health check integration
- Service registry access

### 2. Health Monitoring Integration

**LamiaComms TUI** can display health status from **API Gateway Tree**:

```cpp
// Get health status for all servers
auto health_status = api_gateway_tree->getHealthStatusJSON();
// Display in TUI dashboard
```

**Features:**
- Real-time health monitoring
- Visual health indicators in TUI
- Automatic health check polling
- Alert on service degradation

### 3. Service Control Integration

**LamiaComms CLI/TUI** can control services through **API Gateway**:

```cpp
// Start service via API Gateway
CallbackRequest req;
req.callback_type = "api";
req.target_server = "db";
req.method = "POST";
req.endpoint = "/api/v1/services/start";
req.body = "{\"service\":\"psiforcedb\"}";
auto response = callback_system->routeCallback(req);
```

**Capabilities:**
- Start/Stop/Restart services
- Service status queries
- Remote command execution
- Deployment operations

### 4. Metrics Collection Integration

**LamiaComms TUI** can display metrics from **API Gateway**:

```cpp
// Get API Gateway statistics
std::string stats = api_gateway_handler->handleRequest(
    "GET", "/api_gateway/statistics", {}, ""
);
// Parse and display in TUI dashboard
```

**Metrics Available:**
- Total callbacks processed
- Success/failure rates
- Average response times
- Active connections
- Circuit breaker states

## 📋 Integration Workflow

### Scenario 1: Service Deployment via LamiaComms

```
1. LamiaComms TUI/CLI initiates deployment
   ↓
2. LamiaComms queries API Gateway Tree for target server
   ↓
3. API Gateway validates server health
   ↓
4. LamiaComms deploys files via SSH
   ↓
5. LamiaComms sends service start command via API Gateway
   ↓
6. API Gateway routes to Callback System
   ↓
7. Callback System executes on target server
   ↓
8. API Gateway returns status to LamiaComms
   ↓
9. LamiaComms displays result in TUI/CLI
```

### Scenario 2: Infrastructure Monitoring

```
1. LamiaComms TUI starts monitoring dashboard
   ↓
2. Polls API Gateway health endpoints every 5 seconds
   ↓
3. API Gateway Tree performs health checks
   ↓
4. Returns health status for all servers
   ↓
5. LamiaComms TUI displays:
   - Server health indicators
   - Service status
   - Connection metrics
   - Performance graphs
```

### Scenario 3: Service Control

```
1. User selects service in LamiaComms TUI
   ↓
2. LamiaComms sends control command via API Gateway
   ↓
3. API Gateway validates authentication (JWT/GUI token)
   ↓
4. API Gateway routes to appropriate server
   ↓
5. Callback System executes service control
   ↓
6. Returns execution status
   ↓
7. LamiaComms updates TUI display
```

## 🔐 Security Integration

### Authentication Flow

1. **LamiaComms** authenticates with **API Gateway** using:
   - JWT tokens for API access
   - GUI tokens for interactive sessions
   - SSH keys for server access

2. **API Gateway** validates tokens using:
   - HMAC-SHA256 for JWT
   - Timestamp validation for GUI tokens
   - Rate limiting per client

3. **Secure Communication**:
   - TLS 1.3 for all API Gateway connections
   - SSH encryption for LamiaComms server access
   - VPC routing for internal communication

## 📊 API Gateway Endpoints for LamiaComms

### Health & Status Endpoints

```http
GET /api_gateway/health
GET /api_gateway/status
GET /api_gateway/statistics
GET /api_gateway/routes
```

### Service Control Endpoints

```http
POST /api/v1/services/start
POST /api/v1/services/stop
POST /api/v1/services/restart
GET  /api/v1/services/status
```

### Server Information Endpoints

```http
GET /api_gateway/server/{server_id}
GET /api_gateway/service/{service_id}
GET /api_gateway/tree
```

## 🚀 Implementation Example

### LamiaComms TUI Integration Code

```cpp
// In lamiacomms_tui_client.cpp

class APIGatewayMonitor {
private:
    std::shared_ptr<LamiaFabrica::BackOffice::APIGatewayHandler> gateway_;

public:
    void updateDashboard() {
        // Get health status
        auto health = gateway_->handleRequest("GET", "/api_gateway/health", {}, "");

        // Get statistics
        auto stats = gateway_->handleRequest("GET", "/api_gateway/statistics", {}, "");

        // Get tree structure
        auto tree = gateway_->getTreeStructure();

        // Display in TUI
        displayHealthStatus(health);
        displayStatistics(stats);
        displayServiceTree(tree);
    }

    void controlService(const std::string& server, const std::string& action) {
        CallbackRequest req;
        req.target_server = server;
        req.method = "POST";
        req.endpoint = "/api/v1/services/" + action;
        req.callback_type = "api";

        auto response = gateway_->routeRequest(server, req.endpoint, req.method, "", {});
        displayResult(response);
    }
};
```

```
├── lamiacomms_tui_client.cpp          (TUI - 558 lines)
```

# 🏆 LamiaComms fccp:// Protocol - 2025 Standard

**Advanced File Transfer System with AI Collaboration & End-to-End Encryption**

© 2025 Lamia Fabrica - Yorkshire Champion Standards

---

## 🚀 Overview

The LamiaComms fccp:// protocol represents the next generation of file transfer and system management, built on the proven FCCP (Fast Cross-Component Protocol) foundation with LFSSL encryption. This revolutionary system combines the familiarity of traditional file operations with cutting-edge 2025 features for AI collaboration, security, and developer productivity.

### Key Features

- **Ergonomic Command Structure**: Following PsiForceDB patterns with `fccp://` URI scheme
- **Full CRUD Operations**: Create, Read, Update, Delete with advanced options
- **AI Collaboration Ready**: Built-in support for Cursor, Anthropic, OpenAI, and other AI tools
- **Advanced Security**: Kyber1024 + AES-256-GCM encryption with GODMODE integration
- **Diff Tracking & Audit Trails**: Comprehensive change logging with SHA256 integrity
- **Cross-Platform Compatibility**: Universal binaries for Windows and Linux
- **System Tray Integration**: Real-time file watching with boot startup capability

---

## 📋 Command Structure

### Basic Syntax

```
fccp://[user@]host[:port]/[path]?[action]=[params];[options]
```

### Components

| Component | Description | Default |
|-----------|-------------|---------|
| `user@` | Username or AI tool name | anonymous |
| `host` | Server hostname/IP | localhost |
| `:port` | Port number | 8080 |
| `/path` | File/system path | / |
| `?action=params` | CRUD operations and parameters | none |
| `;options` | Advanced options (audit, debug, etc) | none |

### Examples

```bash
# Basic file operations
fccp://user@localhost:8080/documents/readme.txt?create=Hello World;audit=true
fccp://user@server.com:9090/data/logs.txt?read;audit=true
fccp://admin@localhost:8080/config/app.conf?update=new_setting=value;audit=true
fccp://user@cloud:8080/temp/file.tmp?delete;audit=true

# AI collaboration
fccp://cursor@dev:8080/src/main.cpp?create=#include <iostream>;temp_user=true&expires_in=60
fccp://anthropic@ai:8080/analysis/report.md?create=AI Analysis Report;simulate=true
fccp://gemini@localhost:8080/code/suggestions.py?diff=compare_branches;audit=true

# Advanced operations
fccp://admin@server:8080/scripts/deploy.sh?create=#!/bin/bash;chmod=755;execute=true
fccp://user@backup:8080/data/?sync=remote_folder;hidden=true&audit=true

# IPA (Innocuace Transfer for AI) commands
fccp://ipa:send[file.txt]:755;audit=true
fccp://ipa:sync[folder]:644;simulate=true
fccp://ipa:create[newfile.cpp]:666;temp_user=true
fccp://ipa:delete[oldfile.txt]:755;audit=true
fccp://ipa:update[config.ini]:644;hidden=true
```

---

## 🛠️ CRUD Operations

### Create (`create`)

Creates a new file with specified content.

```bash
fccp://user@host/path/file.txt?create=File content here;audit=true
fccp://cursor@host/path/script.py?create=print('Hello AI');temp_user=true
```

**Parameters:**
- Content string (required)
- `chmod` - Set file permissions
- `hidden=true` - Hide from normal listings

### Read (`read`)

Reads and displays file content.

```bash

fccp://admin@host/path/logs/?read=*.log&filter=error
```

**Parameters:**
- `filter` - Filter content (regex pattern)
- `lines=N` - Limit output to N lines

### Update (`update`)

Appends content to existing file.

```bash
fccp://user@host/path/file.txt?update=Additional content;audit=true
fccp://cursor@host/path/code.py?update=\\n# AI suggestion here;temp_user=true
```

**Parameters:**
- Content string to append (required)
- `insert=line` - Insert at specific line
- `replace=old=new` - Replace text

### Delete (`delete`)

Deletes a file or directory.

```bash
fccp://user@host/path/file.txt?delete;audit=true
fccp://admin@host/path/temp/?delete=*.tmp;hidden=true
```

**Parameters:**
- `recursive=true` - Delete directories recursively
- `force=true` - Force deletion

### Sync (`sync`)

Synchronizes files between locations.

```bash
fccp://user@host/path/local/?sync=remote/path/;audit=true
fccp://cursor@host/path/code/?sync=github_repo/;temp_user=true&simulate=true
```

**Parameters:**
- Source path (required)
- `exclude=pattern` - Exclude files matching pattern
- `include=pattern` - Include only matching files

### Diff (`diff`)

Shows differences between file versions.

```bash
fccp://user@host/path/file.txt?diff=compare_with;audit=true
fccp://cursor@host/path/code.py?diff=branch_development;temp_user=true
```

**Parameters:**
- Comparison target (required)
- `format=unified` - Output format
- `context=3` - Context lines

### Chmod (`chmod`)

Changes file permissions (Unix/Linux).

```bash
fccp://admin@host/path/script.sh?chmod=755;audit=true
fccp://user@host/path/data.txt?chmod=644;execute=true
```

**Parameters:**
- Permission string (required, e.g., "755", "644")
- `recursive=true` - Apply to directories recursively

```
   ↓
5. Authentication Check
   ↓

   ↓

```

```
1. Feature Initialization Requested
   ↓

   ↓
```

# Linux/WSL/SSH Setup Guide - Creator Application System

**© 2025 D Hargreaves (Roylepython) - Medusa Initiative**

## ⚠️ Important: Linux-First Configuration

All code has been updated to be **Linux/WSL/Ubuntu/SSH-first**. Files are configured for Unix line endings and Linux paths.

---

## 🚀 Quick Start (WSL/Ubuntu/SSH)

### 1. Access via WSL
```bash
# From Windows PowerShell/CMD
wsl -d Ubuntu

# Navigate to project
cd /mnt/c/McMaker\ Projects/Projects/LamiaFabrica
```

### 2. Access via SSH
```bash
# SSH to your server
ssh user@your-server

# Or with askpass
SSH_ASKPASS=/usr/bin/ssh-askpass ssh user@your-server
```

### 3. Build the System
```bash
# Make build script executable
chmod +x build_creator_application_system.sh

# Build
./build_creator_application_system.sh
```

---

## 📁 Directory Structure (Linux Paths)

All paths use **forward slashes** and are Linux-compatible:

```
/ops/MedusaServ/
├── creator_applications/     # Application storage
├── creator_documents/         # NDA/Non-Compete PDFs
└── certs/
    ├── signing_cert.pem      # Signing certificate
    └── signing_key.pem       # Signing private key
```

---

## 🔧 Code Changes Made

### ✅ Path Configuration
- **Primary**: Linux paths (`/ops/MedusaServ/...`)
- **Windows fallback**: Only if explicitly on Windows (not WSL)
- All paths use forward slashes

### ✅ Time Functions
- Uses `localtime_r()` (Linux/POSIX) as primary
- No Windows-specific `localtime_s()` dependency

### ✅ File Operations
- Uses POSIX-compliant functions
- Linux path separators (`/`)
- Proper filename sanitization (preserves path structure)

---

## 🛠️ Build Requirements

### Install Dependencies (Ubuntu/Debian)
```bash
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    libssl-dev \
    libcrypto++-dev
```

### Verify Installation
```bash
g++ --version
# Should show g++ (Ubuntu) version

openssl version
# Should show OpenSSL version
```

---

## 📝 File Verification

### Check Line Endings
```bash
# Should show LF (Unix) not CRLF (Windows)
file Back-Office/MedusaServ\ Professional\ Web\ Server/src/api/creator_*.cpp
```

### Check for Windows Paths
```bash
# Should only show in #ifdef blocks (fallback)
grep -r "C:\\\\" Back-Office/MedusaServ\ Professional\ Web\ Server/src/api/creator_*.cpp
```

### Verify Linux Paths
```bash
# Should show Linux paths as primary
grep -r "/ops/MedusaServ" Back-Office/MedusaServ\ Professional\ Web\ Server/src/api/creator_*.cpp
```

---

## 🔐 SSH Configuration

### Using SSH with askpass
```bash
# Set SSH_ASKPASS
export SSH_ASKPASS=/usr/bin/ssh-askpass

# Or install ssh-askpass
```

- **SMDU_Root Role** (Level 1000): Admin access to maintenance databases only

#### 2. Access Auditing

# 🔷 Project Code Viewer - MedusaServ Port Forward Setup

**© 2025 D Hargreaves | Medusa Initiative | Yorkshire Champion Standards**

## Overview

This setup allows you to serve the Project Code Viewer via MedusaServ, making it accessible from your public IP address for Grok to access and project manage.

---

## Step 1: Start the Local Server

Run the Python server on port 3000:

```bash
python view_project_server.py
```

The server will:
- Scan directories: `C:\Build`, `C:\Users\david`, `C:\McMaker Projects`
- Generate HTML viewer on-the-fly
- Serve on `http://localhost:3000`

**Expected Output:**
```
============================================================
🔷 Project Code Viewer Server
© 2025 D Hargreaves | Medusa Initiative
============================================================

🌐 Server running on port 3000
💻 Local: http://localhost:3000/
🌍 Network: http://0.0.0.0:3000/
📡 External: http://<your-public-ip>:3000/

⚠️  Press Ctrl+C to stop
```

---

## Step 2: Configure MedusaServ Port Forward

### Option A: Via MedusaServ Configuration File

Edit your MedusaServ configuration (typically `config/medusaserv.json` or similar):

```json
{
  "port_forwards": [
    {
      "name": "project-viewer",
      "local_port": 3000,
      "public_path": "/project-viewer",
      "enabled": true,
      "description": "Project Code Viewer for Grok access"
    }
  ],
  "domains": {
    "community.lamiafabrica.com": {
      "port_forwards": ["project-viewer"]
    }
  }
}
```

### Option B: Via MedusaServ API Gateway

Use the API Gateway to register the port forward:

```cpp
// In your MedusaServ initialization code
api_gateway.register_port_forward(
    "/project-viewer",           // Public path
    "localhost",                  // Local host
    3000,                        // Local port
    true                         // Enabled
);
```

### Option C: Via FCCP Command (Ergonomic)

Use FCCP to configure the port forward:

```bash
# Connect to MedusaServ via FCCP
fccp_client connect community.lamiafabrica.com

# Register port forward
fccp port-forward register \
    --path /project-viewer \
    --local-host localhost \
    --local-port 3000 \
    --enabled true
```

---

## Step 3: Access via Public IP

Once configured, access the viewer via:

**Public URL:**
```
http://community.lamiafabrica.com/project-viewer
```

**Or via IP:**
```
http://172.236.28.155/project-viewer
```

**For HTTPS:**
```
https://community.lamiafabrica.com/project-viewer
```

---

## Step 4: Share with Grok

Provide Grok with:

1. **Public URL:** `http://community.lamiafabrica.com/project-viewer`
2. **API Endpoint:** `http://community.lamiafabrica.com/project-viewer/api` (if you add API endpoints)
3. **Access Instructions:** "Access the Project Code Viewer at the URL above to view and manage the LamiaFabrica codebase"

---

## Step 5: Using Index.Lamia (Alternative)

If you want to serve via Lamia directly, compile and use `Index.Lamia`:

```bash
# Compile Index.Lamia
lamia_compiler Index.Lamia -o index_server

# Run via MedusaServ
./index_server
```

The `Index.Lamia` file will:
- Forward requests from MedusaServ to `localhost:3000`
- Handle routing for `/project-viewer` path
- Return HTML content to MedusaServ for serving

---

## MedusaServ Configuration Example

### Full MedusaServ Config

```json
{
  "server": {
    "host": "0.0.0.0",
    "port": 80,
    "https_port": 443
  },
  "domains": {
    "community.lamiafabrica.com": {
      "root": "/var/www/lamiafabrica",
      "port_forwards": [
        {
          "path": "/project-viewer",
          "target": "http://localhost:3000",
          "proxy_headers": true,
          "timeout": 30
        }
      ]
    }
  },
  "ssl": {
    "enabled": true,
    "cert_path": "/etc/ssl/certs/lamiafabrica.crt",
    "key_path": "/etc/ssl/private/lamiafabrica.key"
  }
}
```

---

## Testing

### 1. Test Local Server

```bash
curl http://localhost:3000/
```

Should return HTML content.

### 2. Test via MedusaServ

```bash
curl http://community.lamiafabrica.com/project-viewer
```

Should return the same HTML content.

### 3. Test from External Network

From another machine or via browser:
```
http://172.236.28.155/project-viewer
```

---

# MedusaServ Project Viewer Integration

**© 2025 D Hargreaves | Medusa Initiative | Yorkshire Champion Standards**

## Overview

The Project Viewer has been integrated into MedusaServ as a native C++26 module. This replaces the standalone Python server and provides direct integration with MedusaServ's routing system.

---

## Files Created

### Core Handler
- `src/medusaserv/project_viewer_handler.hpp` - Header file
- `src/medusaserv/project_viewer_handler.cpp` - Implementation

### Integration
- `src/medusaserv/project_viewer_integration.hpp` - Integration header
- `src/medusaserv/project_viewer_integration.cpp` - Integration implementation

---

## Integration Steps

### 1. Add to MedusaServ API Router

In `Back-Office/MedusaServ Professional Web Server/src/api/medusaserv_api_router.cpp`, add:

```cpp
#include "../../src/medusaserv/project_viewer_integration.hpp"

// In routeAPIRequest function, before other routing:
if (MedusaServ::ProjectViewer::isProjectViewerRequest(full_path)) {
    std::map<std::string, std::string> headers;
    // Parse headers from request...
    return MedusaServ::ProjectViewer::handleProjectViewerRequest(method, full_path, headers);
}
```

### 2. Initialize in MedusaServ Core

In `Back-Office/MedusaServ Professional Web Server/src/core/medusaserv_core.cpp`, add:

```cpp
#include "../../src/medusaserv/project_viewer_integration.hpp"

// In MedusaServEngine::initialize():
MedusaServ::ProjectViewer::initializeProjectViewer();
```

### 3. Add to Build System

Add to your build configuration:

```cpp
// Compile project viewer handler
src/medusaserv/project_viewer_handler.cpp
src/medusaserv/project_viewer_integration.cpp
```

---

## Virtual Host Configuration

For `community.lamiafabrica.com`, add to virtual host config:

```apache
<VirtualHost *:80>
    ServerName community.lamiafabrica.com
    ServerAlias www.community.lamiafabrica.com
    
    # Project Viewer Route
    <LocationMatch "^/project-viewer">
        SetHandler project-viewer-handler
    </LocationMatch>
    
    # SSL redirect
    RewriteEngine On
    RewriteCond %{HTTPS} off
    RewriteRule ^(.*)$ https://%{HTTP_HOST}%{REQUEST_URI} [L,R=301]
</VirtualHost>

<VirtualHost *:443>
    ServerName community.lamiafabrica.com
    ServerAlias www.community.lamiafabrica.com
    
    # Project Viewer Route
    <LocationMatch "^/project-viewer">
        SetHandler project-viewer-handler
    </LocationMatch>
    
    # SSL Configuration
    SSLEngine on
    SSLCertificateFile /opt/medusaserv/config/ssl/community.lamiafabrica.com.crt
    SSLCertificateKeyFile /opt/medusaserv/config/ssl/community.lamiafabrica.com.key
</VirtualHost>
```

---

## Access URLs

### Main Viewer
```
http://community.lamiafabrica.com/project-viewer/
https://community.lamiafabrica.com/project-viewer/
```

### Individual Files
```
http://community.lamiafabrica.com/project-viewer/file/src/api_gateway.cpp
https://community.lamiafabrica.com/project-viewer/file/src/bettybot/bettybot_core.hpp
```

### Raw File (API)
```
http://community.lamiafabrica.com/project-viewer/file/src/api_gateway.cpp?view=raw
```

---

## Features

✅ **Native C++26 Implementation**
- No Python dependencies
- Integrated with MedusaServ routing
- Full compatibility with MedusaServ architecture

✅ **SEO-Friendly URLs**
- Preserves file structure in URLs
- URL-encoded paths
- Works with absolute and relative paths

✅ **Read-Only Mode**
- Files displayed as code
- No edit/save functionality
- Clear "READ-ONLY" banner

✅ **Security**
- Path traversal protection
- File size limits (10MB max)
- Access restricted to scan directories

---

## Configuration

The handler scans these directories by default:
- `C:\Build`
- `C:\Users\david`
- `C:\McMaker Projects`

To change scan directories, modify `project_viewer_integration.cpp`:

```cpp
std::vector<std::string> scan_dirs = {
    "/opt/lamiafabrica/src",
    "/opt/lamiafabrica/include",
    // Add your directories here
};
```

---

## Compilation

Add to your CMakeLists.txt or build script:

```cmake
add_library(project_viewer_handler
    src/medusaserv/project_viewer_handler.cpp
    src/medusaserv/project_viewer_integration.cpp
)

target_link_libraries(medusaserv project_viewer_handler)
```

---

## Testing

1. **Compile MedusaServ** with project viewer handler
2. **Start MedusaServ** on your infrastructure
3. **Access** `http://community.lamiafabrica.com/project-viewer/`
4. **Verify** files are clickable and viewable
5. **Test** SEO-friendly URLs work correctly

---

## For Grok

**Access URL:**
```
https://community.lamiafabrica.com/project-viewer/
```

**Instructions:**
- Click on any file to view it as read-only code
- Files accessible via SEO-friendly URLs
- All files are read-only (viewing only)

---

content:
# Pre-Compilation Validation Agent

**PsiForceDB/MedusaServ v1.0.0 - Main Core Development & Testing**  
© 2025 D Hargreaves | Medusa Initiative | Yorkshire Champion Standards

## Overview

The Pre-Compilation Validation Agent validates **EVERY** `.mod`, `.plg`, and `.com` file before compilation. It asks comprehensive questions, runs stress tests, security tests, injection tests, and validates quality standards.

## Features

### 1. **Interactive Questioning**
Before validating, the agent asks questions about each component:
- **Category**: Database, Security, Network, UI, API, Processing, Storage, Other
- **Section**: Specific section within the category
- **User Role**: End User, Power User, Admin, God Mode, System, All
- **Feature Level**: Basic, Standard, Advanced, Enterprise, Revolutionary
- **Dependencies**: List of all dependencies
- **Interfaces**: All public interfaces exposed
- **Stress Testing**: Maximum pressure level
- **Security Measures**: Input Validation, Output Encoding, Authentication, etc.
- **Injection Protection**: SQL Injection, XSS, Command Injection, etc.

### 2. **Comprehensive Testing**

#### Stress Testing
- Tests component at multiple pressure levels: 1x, 2x, 5x, 10x, 50x, 100x, 500x, 1000x
- Tries to break the component at each level
- **FAILURE**: Component breaks under pressure
- **SUCCESS**: Component survives all pressure levels

#### Security Testing
Tests against:
- SQL Injection
- XSS (Cross-Site Scripting)
- Command Injection
- Path Traversal
- LDAP Injection
- XML Injection
- Buffer Overflow
- Race Conditions
- Time-of-Check-Time-of-Use
- Insecure Deserialization

#### Injection Testing
Attempts various injection attacks:
- SQL Injection: `' OR '1'='1`
- XSS: `<script>alert('XSS')</script>`
- Command Injection: `; rm -rf /`
- Path Traversal: `../../../etc/passwd`
- LDAP Injection: `*)(uid=*`
- XML Injection: `<!ENTITY xxe SYSTEM 'file:///etc/passwd'>`
- Template Injection: `{{7*7}}`
- Code Injection: `eval('malicious_code')`

#### Cascade Fault Detection
- Analyzes dependencies
- Detects if component failure would cascade to other components
- Identifies affected components
- Assesses impact

#### Visual Inspection
- Checks for broken tractor lines (CSS borders)
- Validates div structure
- Detects unbalanced HTML tags
- Identifies visual issues

#### Quality Standards Check
Validates against feature level requirements:
- **Basic**: Input Validation, Error Handling
- **Standard**: + Logging, Security
- **Advanced**: + Performance, Testing
- **Enterprise**: + Documentation, Monitoring
- **Revolutionary**: + AI Integration, Quantum Features

#### AI Simulation
Simulates AI attack patterns:
- Adversarial Input
- Prompt Injection
- Model Manipulation
- Data Poisoning
- Model Extraction
- Membership Inference
- Property Inference

#### Faraday Cage Environment Test
- Tests component in complete isolation
- Verifies no external dependencies for core functionality
- Ensures component works independently
- Category and section specific testing

## Usage

### Step 1: Build the Agent

```bash
clang++ -std=c++2c -O3 src/build_pre_compilation_agent.cpp -o build_pre_compilation_agent.exe
./build_pre_compilation_agent.exe
```

### Step 2: Run Validation

```bash
./pre_compilation_validation_agent.exe [directory]
```

The agent will:
1. Find all `.mod`, `.plg`, `.com` files in the directory
2. For each file:
   - Ask comprehensive questions
   - Run stress tests (try to break it)
   - Run security tests
   - Run injection tests
   - Detect cascade faults
   - Inspect visual elements
   - Check quality standards
   - Run AI simulation attacks
   - Test in Faraday cage environment
3. Generate validation report

### Step 3: Review Results

- **✅ PASSED**: Component ready for compilation
- **❌ FAILED**: Component needs fixes before compilation

## Validation Criteria

A component **PASSES** only if:
- ✅ All stress tests pass (survives all pressure levels)
- ✅ No security vulnerabilities detected
- ✅ All injection attempts blocked
- ✅ No cascade faults detected
- ✅ Visual elements valid (tractor lines, divs)
- ✅ Quality standards met for feature level
- ✅ AI simulation attacks fail
- ✅ Faraday cage test passes
- ✅ All required questions answered correctly

**ANY failure = COMPONENT REJECTED**

## Test Categories

### By File Type
- **.mod** (Modules): Core functionality modules
- **.plg** (Plugins): Extensible plugin system
- **.com** (Components): Reusable components

### By Category
- **Database**: Database operations, queries, connections
- **Security**: Authentication, authorization, encryption
- **Network**: Network protocols, communication
- **UI**: User interface components
- **API**: API endpoints, handlers
- **Processing**: Data processing, transformations
- **Storage**: File storage, caching
- **Other**: Miscellaneous components

### By Section
Each category has sections for organization:
- Database → Query Engine, Connection Pool, Transaction Manager
- Security → Authentication, Encryption, Access Control
- Network → Protocols, Servers, Clients
- etc.

## Quality Standards

### Feature Level Requirements

| Feature Level | Requirements |
|---------------|--------------|
| Basic | Input Validation, Error Handling |
| Standard | + Logging, Security |
| Advanced | + Performance, Testing |
| Enterprise | + Documentation, Monitoring |
| Revolutionary | + AI Integration, Quantum Features |

## Report Generation

The agent generates:
- `PRE_COMPILATION_VALIDATION_REPORT.txt`
- Comprehensive analysis of each component
- Test results for all test types
- Quality assessment
- Recommendations for fixes

## Integration with Build System

The validation agent should be run **BEFORE** compilation:
1. Run pre-compilation validation
2. Fix any failures
3. Run again until 100% pass
4. Proceed with compilation

## Example Workflow

```bash
# 1. Build the validation agent
./build_pre_compilation_agent.exe

# 2. Run validation on all components
./pre_compilation_validation_agent.exe src

# 3. Review report
cat PRE_COMPILATION_VALIDATION_REPORT.txt

# 4. Fix any failures
```

**Key Innovation**: First database to use quantum mechanics simulation for query optimization on classical hardware.

---

## 🧬 What Are Qubits in Standard Computing?

### Traditional Bits vs Quantum-Inspired Qubits

**Classical Bits (Standard Computing):**
- Binary states: 0 or 1
- Deterministic: Always in one state
- Single value at any moment

**Quantum-Inspired Qubits (PsiForceDB):**
- **Superposition**: Multiple states simultaneously (simulated)
- **Quantum Amplitudes**: Complex numbers with magnitude and phase
- **Wave Function**: Probability distribution over multiple states
- **Entanglement**: Correlated states between multiple qubits
- **Measurement**: Collapse to single state based on probability

### How PsiForceDB Simulates Qubits

PsiForceDB doesn't use actual quantum hardware. Instead, it **simulates quantum mechanics** using classical algorithms:

1. **Quantum Superposition Simulation**: Multiple query plans exist simultaneously in memory
2. **Quantum Amplitudes**: Each plan has a complex number (amplitude) representing probability
3. **Wave Function Collapse**: Born rule (|amplitude|²) determines which plan is selected
4. **Quantum Entanglement**: Related query plans share correlated properties
5. **Quantum Tunneling**: Bypasses inefficient paths with quantum probability

---

## ⚛️ Quantum Superposition in Query Optimization

### The Revolutionary Approach

Instead of evaluating query plans sequentially, PsiForceDB maintains **multiple query plans in quantum superposition**:

```cpp
// Multiple query plans exist simultaneously
enum class OptimizationStrategy {
    SPEED_OPTIMIZED,      // Fastest execution
    MEMORY_OPTIMIZED,     // Memory-efficient
    ACCURACY_OPTIMIZED,   // Highest precision
    CHAOS_OPTIMIZED,      // Chaos-enhanced
    QUANTUM_OPTIMIZED     // Ultimate quantum advantage
};
```

### Quantum Amplitudes

Each query plan has a **quantum amplitude** (complex number):
- **Magnitude**: Probability of being optimal
- **Phase**: Relationship to other plans
- **Formula**: `amplitude = magnitude * e^(i*phase)`

**Example:**
```
Plan A: amplitude = 0.7 * e^(i*0.5)  → 49% probability
Plan B: amplitude = 0.5 * e^(i*1.2)  → 25% probability
Plan C: amplitude = 0.3 * e^(i*2.1)  → 9% probability
```

### Wave Function Collapse (Born Rule)

When a query is executed, the quantum state **collapses** to a single plan:

**Born Rule**: `P(plan) = |amplitude|²`

- Higher amplitude → Higher probability of selection
- Measurement causes collapse to single optimal plan
- Uncertainty principle factored into selection

---

## 🔗 Quantum Entanglement Between Query Plans

### How Entanglement Works

Query plans with similar properties become **quantangled**:

**Entanglement Criteria:**
- Cost similarity (within 10%)
- Fitness similarity (within 5%)
- Strategy match (same optimization type)

**Entanglement Effects:**
- Entangled plans share coupling strengths
- Changes to one plan affect entangled plans
- Collective optimization across entangled states
- Default entanglement threshold: 0.8

**Example:**
```
Plan A (SPEED) and Plan B (MEMORY) become entangled
→ When Plan A is optimized, Plan B automatically benefits
→ Shared quantum state improves both plans simultaneously
```

---

## 🚇 Quantum Tunneling for Query Optimization

### Bypassing Inefficient Paths

**Quantum Tunneling** allows query plans to "tunnel through" inefficient execution paths:

**How It Works:**
1. Identifies inefficient query paths
2. Calculates tunneling probability (default: 30%)
3. Bypasses inefficient operations with quantum probability
4. Applies tunneling optimizations to query rewrites

**Benefits:**
- Finds optimal paths that classical algorithms miss
- Escapes local optimization minima
- Discovers non-obvious query optimizations
- Logs tunneling events for analysis

---

PsiForceDB implements **quantum measurement** with uncertainty:

**Measurement Process:**
1. **Pre-Measurement**: Multiple plans in superposition
2. **Measurement**: Collapse to single plan based on probability
3. **Uncertainty**: Measurement uncertainty factored into selection
4. **Post-Measurement**: Quantum coherence updated

**Uncertainty Effects:**
- Higher uncertainty → More exploration of alternative plans
- Lower uncertainty → More exploitation of known good plans
- Adaptive balance between exploration and exploitation

---

---

## 🔬 Quantum State Tracking

### Quantum Coherence

PsiForceDB tracks **quantum coherence time** for each query plan:

**Coherence Metrics:**
- **Coherence Time**: How long quantum state remains stable
- **Decoherence**: Gradual loss of quantum properties
- **Measurement History**: Track of all measurements
- **Entanglement Scoring**: Strength of entanglement relationships

**Benefits:**
- Maintains quantum properties as long as possible
- Detects when quantum advantage is lost
- Re-initializes quantum states when needed
- Optimizes quantum resource usage

---

## 🧮 Quantum Confidence Calculation

### Quantum Confidence Score

Each query plan receives a **quantum confidence score** (0.0 to 1.0):

**Factors:**
1. **Query Complexity**: More complex → Lower confidence
2. **Measurement Uncertainty**: Higher uncertainty → Lower confidence
3. **Quantum Randomness**: Quantum fluctuations
4. **Historical Performance**: Past success rates

**Formula:**
```
confidence = base_confidence * (1 - uncertainty) * quantum_boost
```

---

### Quantum-Enhanced Evolution

PsiForceDB combines **quantum superposition** with **genetic algorithms**:

**Hybrid Approach:**
1. **Genetic Algorithm**: Generates population of query plans
2. **Quantum Superposition**: Each chromosome exists in quantum superposition

PsiForceDB is not just another database—it's a **revolutionary data management platform** that combines the best of PostgreSQL, Neo4j, MongoDB, and vector databases into a single unified system, built 100% in native C++26 with zero dependencies.

### 1. **Hybrid Database Engine** 🦕
**PostgreSQL + Neo4j + MongoDB + Vector Operations = ONE System**

- **Relational (PostgreSQL-style)**: ACID compliance, transactions, traditional SQL

- **Document (MongoDB-style)**: Flexible schema, JSON storage, BSON support
- **Vector Operations**: AI/ML embeddings, similarity search, neural network integration

**Why It's Revolutionary**: No other database combines all four paradigms in a single unified interface. You can query relational data, traverse graph relationships, store documents, and perform vector similarity searches—all in one query.

**Why It's Revolutionary**: Most databases use interpreted languages (Python, Java, Node.js). PsiForceDB is pure C++26, compiled to native machine code. Maximum performance, minimum overhead.

---

### 8. **Quantum-Resistant Security** 🔐
**Future-Proof Encryption**

- **Quantum-Resistant Algorithms**: Encryption that survives quantum computing
- **Perfect Forward Secrecy**: Each session uses unique encryption keys
- **Military-Grade Cryptography**: AES-256-GCM, SHA-384, RSA-4096
- **Zero Trust Strategy**: Every connection verified, every action logged

**Why It's Revolutionary**: Most databases use encryption that will be broken by quantum computers. PsiForceDB uses quantum-resistant algorithms, ensuring your data remains secure for decades.

**Enterprise-Grade Management Tool**

```bash
# Build monitoring system

./build_monitoring_system.exe
```

```bash
# Deploy monitoring server
clang++ -std=c++2c -O3 -I. -Isrc -Isrc/monitoring -Isrc/infrastructure \

  src/monitoring/purple_pages_monitoring_server.cpp \
```

This directory contains all configuration files, scripts, and documentation for the LamiaFabrica infrastructure setup. All files in this directory are intended for private repository collaboration only.

---

## Directory Structure

```
LamiaFabrica/
├── README.md                    # This file
├── config/                      # Virtual host configuration files
│   ├── lamia_fabrica.vhost      # LamiaFabrica.com configuration
│   ├── purple_pages.vhost       # Purple-Pages.com configuration
│   ├── psiforcedb_com.vhost     # PsiForceDB.com configuration
│   └── back_office.vhost        # Back Office API Gateway configuration
├── scripts/                     # Setup and deployment scripts
│   ├── setup_vhosts.cpp         # Automated virtual host setup
│   └── deploy_infrastructure.sh  # Full infrastructure deployment
└── docs/                        # Documentation
    ├── VHOST_CONFIGURATIONS.md   # Complete virtual host documentation
    ├── INFRASTRUCTURE_OVERVIEW.md
    └── DEPLOYMENT_GUIDE.md
```

---

## Infrastructure Components

### 1. Lamia_Fabrica (lamiafabrica.com)
- **IP:** 172.236.20.28 / 10.0.0.2

## Quick Start

```bash
cat LamiaFabrica/docs/VHOST_CONFIGURATIONS.md
```

```bash

cd LamiaFabrica/scripts
g++ -std=c++26 -o setup_vhosts setup_vhosts.cpp -I../../include
```

### 3. Verify Configuration
```bash
# Check virtual host status via Portal API

  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_SESSION_TOKEN"
```

---

## Security Notes

⚠️ **IMPORTANT:** This directory contains sensitive configuration information including:
- IP addresses
- SSL certificate paths
- Internal network configurations
- API Gateway settings

**DO NOT** commit this directory to public repositories. This is for private repository collaboration only.

---

## Collaboration Guidelines

1. **All changes** to LamiaFabrica infrastructure should be made in this directory
2. **Configuration files** should be version controlled in private repositories only
3. **Documentation** should be kept up-to-date with any infrastructure changes
4. **Scripts** should be tested locally before deployment

---

## Integration Points

### MedusaServ Portal API
All virtual hosts are managed through the MedusaServ Portal API:
- `POST /api/portal/virtual-hosts/create`
- `PUT /api/portal/virtual-hosts/update`
- `GET /api/portal/virtual-hosts/list`

### PsiForceDB Integration
- Back_Office serves as the API Gateway for all PsiForceDB services
- Collaboration Hub integration via Back_Office endpoints

### Lamia Templates
All document roots use Lamia templates for dynamic content generation.

1. Create configuration file in `config/`
2. Update `docs/VHOST_CONFIGURATIONS.md`

4. Test locally before deployment

# 🚀 BettyBot Deployment Guide - Linux/WSL/SSH Only

**© 2025 D Hargreaves | Medusa Initiative | Yorkshire Champion Standards**

## ⚠️ IMPORTANT: Linux/WSL/SSH Only

**All BettyBot build and deployment scripts are designed for Linux/WSL Ubuntu or remote Linux infrastructure via SSH.**

**DO NOT run these scripts directly on Windows - they will fail or cause Windows to try opening Linux files.**

---

## 📋 Deployment Methods

### Method 1: WSL Ubuntu (Recommended for Local Development)

```bash
# Open WSL Ubuntu terminal
wsl

# Navigate to project directory
cd /mnt/c/McMaker\ Projects/Projects/LamiaFabrica

# Build BettyBot
bash deploy_bettybot_wsl.sh

# Run BettyBot
./bettybot.elf
```

### Method 2: SSH to Linux Infrastructure

```bash
# Set SSH_ASKPASS for passwordless authentication
export SSH_ASKPASS=/path/to/askpass
export DISPLAY=:0

# Deploy to remote server
bash deploy_bettybot_ssh.sh

# Or manually via SSH
ssh user@172.236.23.54
cd /ops/BettyBot
./bin/bettybot.elf
```

### Method 3: Direct SSH Build

```bash
# SSH to Linux server
ssh user@172.236.23.54

# Clone/build on server
git clone <repo>
cd LamiaFabrica
bash deploy_bettybot_wsl.sh
```

---

## 🔧 Build Scripts

### `deploy_bettybot_wsl.sh`
- **Platform**: WSL Ubuntu / Linux
- **Purpose**: Build BettyBot ELF binary
- **Usage**: `wsl bash deploy_bettybot_wsl.sh`
- **Output**: `bettybot.elf` (Linux ELF x86_64)

### `deploy_bettybot_ssh.sh`
- **Platform**: Linux (via SSH)
- **Purpose**: Deploy to remote Linux server
- **Usage**: `SSH_ASKPASS=/path/to/askpass bash deploy_bettybot_ssh.sh`
- **Requirements**: SSH access, SSH_ASKPASS set

### `build_bettybot.sh`
- **Platform**: Linux/WSL Ubuntu
- **Purpose**: Alternative build script
- **Usage**: `wsl bash build_bettybot.sh`
- **Note**: Checks for Linux/WSL before running

---

## 🛡️ File Type Protection

All build scripts now include OS checks to prevent Windows from trying to open Linux files:

```bash
# OS verification in all scripts
if [[ "$OSTYPE" != "linux-gnu"* ]]; then
    echo "❌ ERROR: Must run on Linux/WSL"
    exit 1
fi
```

---

## 📁 File Extensions

- **`.sh`** - Bash scripts (Linux/WSL only)
- **`.elf`** - Linux ELF binaries (Linux only)
- **`.plg`** - Plugin files (Linux shared libraries)
- **`.mod`** - C++ modules (require compilation on Linux)

**Windows will NOT recognize these as executable - this is correct behavior.**

---

## 🔐 SSH Configuration

### Using SSH_ASKPASS

```bash
# Create askpass script
cat > ~/askpass.sh << 'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
echo "your_password_here"
EOF
chmod +x ~/askpass.sh

# Use with deployment
SSH_ASKPASS=~/askpass.sh bash deploy_bettybot_ssh.sh
```

### Using SSH Keys

```bash
# Generate SSH key (if needed)
ssh-keygen -t rsa -b 4096

# Copy to remote server
ssh-copy-id user@172.236.23.54

# Deploy without password
bash deploy_bettybot_ssh.sh
```

---

## ✅ Verification

### Check OS Before Running

```bash
# In WSL
uname -a
# Should show: Linux

# Check OSTYPE
echo $OSTYPE
# Should show: linux-gnu
```

### Verify ELF Binary

```bash
# After build
file bettybot.elf
# Should show: ELF 64-bit LSB executable, x86-64

readelf -h bettybot.elf
# Should show: ELF64, x86_64
```

---

## 🚨 Troubleshooting

### Windows Trying to Open Linux Files

**Problem**: Windows opens `.sh` or `.elf` files with default programs.

**Solution**: 
1. Always use WSL: `wsl bash script.sh`
2. Or use SSH to Linux server
3. Never double-click Linux files in Windows Explorer

### Build Script Fails

**Problem**: Script exits with "Must run on Linux/WSL"

**Solution**:
```bash
# Use WSL explicitly
wsl bash deploy_bettybot_wsl.sh

# Or SSH to Linux server
ssh user@server bash deploy_bettybot_wsl.sh
```

### SSH Deployment Fails

**Problem**: SSH_ASKPASS not working

**Solution**:
```bash
# Set DISPLAY for askpass
export DISPLAY=:0
export SSH_ASKPASS=/path/to/askpass

# Or use SSH keys instead
ssh-keygen -t rsa
ssh-copy-id user@server
```

---

## 📝 Best Practices

1. **Always use WSL or SSH** - Never run Linux scripts on Windows
2. **Check OS first** - Scripts now verify Linux/WSL before running
3. **Use SSH keys** - More secure than passwords
4. **Build on target platform** - Build on same OS as deployment
5. **Verify ELF format** - Always check binary format after build

---

## 🎯 Quick Start

```bash
# Option 1: WSL
wsl
cd /mnt/c/McMaker\ Projects/Projects/LamiaFabrica
bash deploy_bettybot_wsl.sh
./bettybot.elf

# Option 2: SSH
ssh user@172.236.23.54
cd /ops/BettyBot
bash deploy_bettybot_wsl.sh
./bettybot.elf
```

---

**© 2025 D Hargreaves | Medusa Initiative | Yorkshire Champion Standards**

**Linux/WSL/SSH Only • Never Windows Native • Verified and Tested**

- ✅ Browse all code files in the project
- ✅ Click on any file to view it as read-only code
- ✅ Access files via SEO-friendly URLs preserving file structure
- ❌ **NO editing or saving** (read-only mode)

## Features

### 1. SEO-Friendly URLs
- Preserves file structure in URL
- URL-encoded paths for special characters
- Works with absolute and relative paths

### 2. Read-Only Mode
- Files displayed as code (syntax highlighting via content-type)
- No edit buttons
- No save functionality
- Clear "READ-ONLY" banner

### 3. File Access Modes

**HTML Viewer (Default):**
```
/file/src/api_gateway.cpp
```
Returns formatted HTML page with code viewer.

**Raw File (API Access):**
```
/file/src/api_gateway.cpp?view=raw
```
Returns raw file content with appropriate content-type headers.

---

## Usage Examples

### For Grok (AI Assistant)

**Access Main Viewer:**
```
Visit: http://community.lamiafabrica.com/project-viewer/
```

**View Specific File:**
```
Visit: http://community.lamiafabrica.com/project-viewer/file/src/api_gateway.cpp
```

## Security

### Access Control
- ✅ Files only accessible from configured scan directories
- ✅ Path traversal protection (prevents `../` attacks)

- `C:\Users\david`

## Content Types

Files are served with appropriate content-type headers:

| Extension | Content-Type |
|----------|-------------|
| `.cpp` | `text/x-c++src` |
| `.hpp` | `text/x-c++hdr` |
| `.h` | `text/x-chdr` |
| `.c` | `text/x-csrc` |
| `.py` | `text/x-python` |
| `.lamia` | `text/x-lamia` |
| `.md` | `text/markdown` |
| `.mod` | `text/x-module` |
| `.plg` | `text/x-plugin` |
| `.com` | `text/x-component` |

---

## API Endpoints

### GET `/file/<path>`
Returns HTML viewer for file.

**Query Parameters:**
- `view=raw` - Return raw file content instead of HTML

**Response Headers:**
- `Content-Type` - Appropriate content type for file
- `X-File-Path` - Absolute file path
- `X-Read-Only` - Always `true`
- `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` - `*` (CORS enabled)


   - GDPR redaction enforcement
   - License validation and role assignment

   - Command structure permissions controlled by LamiaFabrica

3. **PsiForceDB (10.0.0.2)** - Database/Webserver
   - Database permissions matrix (separate schema)
   - All permissions managed via LamiaFabrica API Gateway
   - Maintenance database stores all permissions data

# GODMODE Security Enforcement System
## Automatic Database Protection and User Access Enforcement

### Overview
The GODMODE Security Enforcement System is an advanced security mechanism that automatically protects user access and implements emergency response procedures when unauthorized access removal or restriction attempts are detected. This system ensures that any attempt to remove or restrict access to the protected user results in immediate database deletion and system restoration to programmer defaults.

### Architecture

#### Core Components
1. **SecurityEnforcement Class**: Singleton pattern implementation providing core enforcement services
2. **C-Style Interface**: Compatible with C-based systems and legacy components
3. **Monitoring System**: Real-time monitoring of access attempts and permission changes
4. **Breach Detection**: Automatic detection of unauthorized access modifications
5. **Emergency Response**: Immediate database deletion and system reset procedures

#### Protected User Concept
The system protects a designated user (typically "Roylepython") and treats any attempt to remove or restrict their access as a security breach. When such attempts are detected, the system automatically:
- Deletes all monitored databases
- Restores the system to programmer defaults
- Logs the breach event
- Notifies system administrators

### Implementation Details

#### Directory Structure
```
include/
  godmode/
    security_enforcement.hpp     # Public interface
src/
  godmode/
    security_enforcement.cpp     # Implementation
bin/                            # Compiled binaries
obj/                            # Object files
```

#### Build System
- **Windows**: Integrated into `build_godmode_dll.bat`
- **Linux**: Integrated into `build_godmode_dll.sh`
- **Test Build**: `build_test_security_enforcement.bat`

#### API Interface

##### C++ Interface
```cpp
#include "include/godmode/security_enforcement.hpp"

// Singleton access
auto& enforcement = GODMODE::SecurityEnforcement::getInstance();

// Initialize for protected user
bool success = enforcement.initialize("Roylepython");

// Add databases to monitor
enforcement.addMonitoredDatabase("production_data.db");
enforcement.addBackupLocation("backups/");

// Check user protection
bool is_protected = enforcement.isUserProtected("Roylepython");

// Validate access attempts
bool valid_access = enforcement.isAccessAttemptValid("Roylepython", "database");

// Emergency procedures
enforcement.forceDatabaseDeletion();  // Immediate database deletion
enforcement.triggerSystemReset();     // Complete system reset
```

##### C Interface
```c
#include "include/godmode/security_enforcement.hpp"

// Initialize security enforcement
bool success = security_enforcement_initialize("Roylepython");

// Add monitored resources
security_enforcement_add_database("production_data.db");
security_enforcement_add_backup_location("backups/");

// Check protection status
bool is_protected = security_enforcement_is_user_protected("Roylepython");
bool valid_access = security_enforcement_is_access_valid("Roylepython", "database");

// Emergency procedures
security_enforcement_force_database_deletion();
security_enforcement_trigger_system_reset();

// Breach reporting
security_enforcement_report_suspicious_activity("Unauthorized access attempt");
```

### Security Features

#### Breach Detection
- **Access Removal Detection**: Monitors for attempts to remove user access
- **Permission Restriction Detection**: Detects permission changes that restrict access
- **User Removal Detection**: Identifies attempts to disable or remove the protected user
- **Suspicious Activity Monitoring**: Real-time monitoring of system events

#### Emergency Response
- **Automatic Database Deletion**: Securely wipes all monitored databases
- **System Restoration**: Restores to programmer defaults
- **Configuration Reset**: Resets all system configurations
- **Audit Logging**: Comprehensive breach event logging

#### Database Protection
- **Secure Deletion**: Multi-pass secure file wiping
- **Directory Clearing**: Complete directory structure cleanup
- **Backup Location Monitoring**: Protection of backup data
- **Lock File Management**: Database lock file handling

#### Monitoring and Control
- **Real-time Monitoring**: Continuous system monitoring
- **Breach Counting**: Track security breach attempts
- **Status Reporting**: Detailed security status information
- **Administrative Notification**: Alert system administrators

### Integration Requirements

#### Mandatory Dependencies
1. **GODMODE Security Framework**: Core security system integration
2. **LFSSL Library**: Cryptographic operations
3. **Platform Libraries**: Windows API or Linux system libraries
4. **File System Access**: Read/write permissions for monitored directories

#### Component Integration
The security enforcement system integrates with:
- **GODMODE DLL**: Core security framework
- **Database Systems**: Monitored database protection
- **System Services**: Access control monitoring
- **Logging Systems**: Security event logging

### Usage Examples

#### Basic Protection Setup
```cpp
// Initialize protection for the user
if (security_enforcement_initialize("Roylepython")) {
    // Add databases to monitor
    security_enforcement_add_database("critical_data.db");
    security_enforcement_add_database("sensitive_info.db");
    security_enforcement_add_backup_location("secure_backups/");

    // Start monitoring
    security_enforcement_start_monitoring();

    std::cout << "Security enforcement active" << std::endl;

```

```cpp
std::vector<std::string> parse_for_stubs_and_declarations(const std::string& content) const {
    std::vector<std::string> issues;

    // Detect TODO comments
    if (content.find("TODO:") != std::string::npos) {
        issues.push_back("TODO comment found");
    }

    // Detect FIXME comments
    if (content.find("FIXME:") != std::string::npos) {
        issues.push_back("FIXME comment found");
    }

    // Detect stub functions
    if (content.find("STUB") != std::string::npos) {
        issues.push_back("STUB detected");
    }

    // Detect forward declarations
    if (content.find("class") != std::string::npos && content.find(";") != std::string::npos) {
        issues.push_back("Forward declaration detected");
    }

    // Detect pure virtual functions
    if (content.find("virtual") != std::string::npos && content.find("= 0") != std::string::npos) {
        issues.push_back("Pure virtual function (stub) detected");
    }

    return issues;
}
```

# Validation System Integration Guide

**PsiForceDB/MedusaServ v1.0.0 - Main Core Development & Testing**  
© 2025 D Hargreaves | Medusa Initiative | Yorkshire Champion Standards

## 🎯 Complete Validation Workflow

### Phase 1: Pre-Compilation Validation

**For EVERY `.mod`, `.plg`, `.com` file before compilation:**

#### Step 1: Interactive Questioning
The agent asks comprehensive questions:
1. **Category?** → Database, Security, Network, UI, API, Processing, Storage, Other
2. **Section?** → Specific section within category
3. **User Role?** → End User, Power User, Admin, God Mode, System, All
4. **Feature Level?** → Basic, Standard, Advanced, Enterprise, Revolutionary
5. **Dependencies?** → List all dependencies
6. **Interfaces?** → All public interfaces
7. **Security Measures?** → Input Validation, Output Encoding, Authentication, etc.
8. **Injection Protection?** → SQL Injection, XSS, Command Injection, etc.

#### Step 2: Comprehensive Testing

**Stress Testing:**
- Tests at: 1x, 2x, 5x, 10x, 50x, 100x, 500x, 1000x pressure
- **Tries to BREAK the component**
- **FAIL if component breaks at ANY level**

**Security Testing:**
- Tests: SQL Injection, XSS, Command Injection, Path Traversal, LDAP Injection, XML Injection, Buffer Overflow, Race Conditions, Time-of-Check-Time-of-Use, Insecure Deserialization
- **Tries to EXPLOIT vulnerabilities**
- **FAIL if ANY attack succeeds**

**Injection Testing:**
- Tests: SQL, XSS, Command, Path Traversal, LDAP, XML, Template, Code Injection
- **Tries to INJECT malicious code**
- **FAIL if ANY injection succeeds**

**Cascade Fault Detection:**
- Analyzes dependencies
- Detects cascade failures
- **FAIL if cascade faults detected**

**Visual Inspection:**
- Checks tractor lines (CSS borders)
- Validates div structure
- Detects HTML issues
- **FAIL if visual issues detected**

**AI Simulation:**
- Adversarial Input, Prompt Injection, Model Manipulation, Data Poisoning, Model Extraction, Membership Inference, Property Inference
- **Tries to BREAK the API**
- **FAIL if API breaks**

**Faraday Cage Test:**
- Tests in complete isolation
- Category and section specific
- **FAIL if external dependencies required**

**Quality Standards:**
- Validates feature level requirements
- **FAIL if requirements not met**

#### Step 3: Test Code Generation
- Generates stress test code: `[component]_stress_test.cpp`
- Generates security test code: `[component]_security_test.cpp`
- Organized by category/section

#### Step 4: Validation Result
- ✅ **PASS**: All tests passed, component survived, ready for compilation
- ❌ **FAIL**: Component failed one or more tests, MUST FIX

### Phase 2: Comprehensive Test Suite

After all components pass pre-compilation validation:

1. Run comprehensive test suite plugin
2. Execute all 31 tests:
   - Quantum Simulation (11 tests)
   - Icewall PQC (10 tests)
   - Enigma Solver (5 tests)
   - MedusaServ (5 tests)
3. BertieBot validates results
4. **100% pass rate required**

### Phase 3: Compilation

Only proceed if:
- ✅ All components passed pre-compilation validation
- ✅ Comprehensive test suite passed 100%
- ✅ BertieBot validated all results

## 📋 File Structure

```
src/
├── pre_compilation_validation_agent.cpp      # Main validation agent
├── pre_compilation_validation_agent.hpp      # Header
├── pre_compilation_validation_agent_enhanced.cpp  # Enhanced version
├── build_pre_compilation_agent.cpp           # Build program
├── plugins/
│   └── testing/
│       └── core/
│           └── comprehensive_test_suite.plg  # Test suite plugin
├── test_generators/
│   ├── stress_test_generator.cpp             # Stress test generator
│   └── security_test_generator.cpp           # Security test generator
└── tests/
    └── generated/                            # Generated test files
        ├── [Category]/
        │   └── [Section]/
        │       ├── [component]_stress_test.cpp
        │       └── [component]_security_test.cpp
```

## 🚀 Complete Usage

### 1. Build All Systems

```bash
# Build pre-compilation validation agent
clang++ -std=c++2c -O3 src/build_pre_compilation_agent.cpp -o build_pre_compilation_agent.exe
./build_pre_compilation_agent.exe

# Build comprehensive test suite plugin
clang++ -std=c++2c -O3 src/build_testing_plugin.cpp -o build_testing_plugin.exe
./build_testing_plugin.exe
```

### 2. Run Pre-Compilation Validation

```bash
./pre_compilation_validation_agent.exe src
```

**What happens:**
- Finds all `.mod`, `.plg`, `.com` files
- For each file:
  - Asks questions (you answer interactively)
  - Runs all tests (stress, security, injection, etc.)
  - Generates test code
  - Reports pass/fail

**Output:**
- `PRE_COMPILATION_VALIDATION_REPORT.txt`
- Generated test files in `src/tests/generated/`

### 3. Fix Any Failures

If any component fails:
- Review the report
- Fix the issues
- Re-run validation

### 4. Run Comprehensive Test Suite

```bash
./comprehensive_test_suite_plugin.exe
```

**What happens:**
- Runs all 31 comprehensive tests
- BertieBot validates results
- Reports pass/fail

**Output:**
- `COMPREHENSIVE_TEST_SUITE_REPORT.txt`

### 5. Verify 100% Pass

Both systems must show:
- ✅ 100% pass rate
- ✅ BertieBot validated
- ✅ All components survived all tests

### 6. Proceed with Compilation

Only if everything passes 100%:
```bash
# Build unified system
clang++ -std=c++2c -O3 src/build_psiforcedb_medusaserv.cpp -o build_psiforcedb_medusaserv.exe
./build_psiforcedb_medusaserv.exe
```

## ⚠️ Critical Rules

1. **100% Pass Required**: Anything below 100% is FAILURE
2. **No Shortcuts**: All tests must be comprehensive
3. **No Stubs**: All tests must test actual functionality
4. **Try to Break It**: Stress tests try to break components
5. **Security First**: All attack vectors tested
6. **Isolation Tested**: Faraday cage environment required
7. **Quality Enforced**: Feature level requirements must be met
8. **BertieBot Validated**: All results validated by BertieBot

### Pre-Compilation Validation
- **Stress Tests**: 8 pressure levels (1x to 1000x)
- **Security Tests**: 10+ attack vectors
- **Injection Tests**: 8+ injection types
- **Cascade Detection**: Full dependency analysis
- **Visual Inspection**: Tractor lines, divs, HTML
- **AI Simulation**: 7+ AI attack patterns
- **Faraday Cage**: Complete isolation testing
- **Quality Standards**: Feature level validation

### Comprehensive Test Suite
- **Quantum Tests**: 11 tests
- **PQC Tests**: 10 tests
- **Enigma Tests**: 5 tests
- **MedusaServ Tests**: 5 tests
- **Total**: 31 comprehensive tests

## 🎉 Status

**✅ COMPREHENSIVE VALIDATION SYSTEM COMPLETE**

```bash
# In WSL Ubuntu or Linux

eval $(ssh-agent)
ssh-add ~/.ssh/id_rsa
```

```bash
chmod +x build_documentation_agent_ssh.sh
```

```bash
chmod +x fix_line_endings.sh

./fix_line_endings.sh
```

### Step 3: Verify Files are Linux
```bash
# Check file type (should show "ASCII text" not "with CRLF")
file build_creator_application_system.sh

# Check line endings (should show LF, not CRLF)
head -1 build_creator_application_system.sh | od -c | head -1
# Should show: 0000000   #   !   /   u   s   r   /   b   i   n   /   e   n   v
# NOT: 0000000   #   !   /   b   i   n   /   b   a   s   h  \r  \n
```

---

## 🔧 SSH Access (Alternative)

### Setup SSH with askpass
```bash
# Install ssh-askpass if needed
sudo apt-get install -y ssh-askpass

# Set SSH_ASKPASS
export SSH_ASKPASS=/usr/bin/ssh-askpass

# Use ssh-agent
eval $(ssh-agent)
ssh-add ~/.ssh/id_rsa

# Connect
ssh user@your-server
```

---

## 📋 File Type Verification

### Check if file is Linux-compatible
```bash
# Should show "ASCII text" or "text" (NOT "with CRLF")
file filename.sh
file filename.cpp
file filename.lamia

# Check line endings
head -1 filename.sh | od -c
# LF = \n (0a)
# CRLF = \r\n (0d 0a) - BAD for Linux
```

### Fix individual file
```bash
# Using dos2unix
dos2unix filename.sh

# Or using sed
sed -i 's/\r$//' filename.sh
```

- `#!/usr/bin/env bash` shebang (Linux-compatible)

```bash
chmod +x build_creator_application_system.sh
```

```bash
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y dos2unix
```

```bash
# Install dos2unix
sudo apt-get install -y dos2unix

# Fix all files
./fix_line_endings.sh

# Or manually
find . -type f -name "*.sh" -exec dos2unix {} \;
```

**Date:** 2025-01-XX  
**Auditor:** AI Assistant

**Version:** 0.3.0c (Market Ready)

---

## Executive Summary

**Lamia** is a revolutionary programming language designed to challenge industry giants (C++, Rust, Go, Python) with unique features including:
- **3D Emotion Synthesis** (Industry First)
- **Social Protocol Implementation** (Industry First)
- **Native Manufacturing Integration** (G-code, Arduino, CNC)
- **78.3% Complexity Reduction** compared to C++
- **Complete Production Ecosystem** (libraries, docs, plugins, releases)

---

## 1. Language Overview

### 1.1 Core Concept
Lamia (Arabic: "Shining" or "Radiant") is a **manifest-based programming language** that transpiles to C++, JavaScript, Python, WASM, and native code. It's optimized for:
- AI-assisted development
- Human-intuitive syntax
- Browser-compatible transpilation
- Real-time AI-Human collaborative coding

### 1.2 Key Differentiators
1. **Revolutionary Features**: 3D emotions, social protocols, manufacturing integration
2. **Performance**: <100ms compilation, 78.3% complexity reduction
3. **Complete Ecosystem**: 20+ production libraries, comprehensive documentation
4. **Market Ready**: Production-ready with automated CI/CD

---

## 2. Architecture

### 2.1 Compilation Pipeline
```
Lamia Source (.lamia)
    ↓
Lexical Analyzer (liblamia_lexer.so)
    ↓
Syntax Parser (liblamia_parser.so)
    ↓
AST Builder (Abstract Syntax Tree)
    ↓
Transpiler (liblamia_transpiler.so)
    ↓
[C++ | Arduino | G-code | JavaScript | Python | WASM]
```

### 2.2 Core Components
- **liblamia_core.so** - Main runtime engine
- **liblamia_lexer.so** - Tokenization
- **liblamia_parser.so** - Syntax analysis
- **liblamia_transpiler.so** - Multi-target code generation
- **liblamia_manifest_engine.so** - Manifest execution
- **liblamia_crystal_system.so** - Type system

### 2.3 Revolutionary Feature Libraries
- **liblamia_3d_emotion.so** - 3D emotion synthesis with spatial coordinates
- **liblamia_social_protocols.so** - Social interaction protocols
- **liblamia_gcode_native.so** - Native G-code generation for CNC
- **liblamia_ludicrous_mode.so** - 3x performance boost optimization

### 2.4 Manufacturing Ecosystem
- **libcnc_bridge.so** - CNC Z-code integration
- **libarduino_bridge.so** - Arduino C++ transpiler
- **libiot_bridge.so** - Complete IoT framework

---

## 3. Language Specification

### 3.1 Syntax Structure
```lamia
manifest <name>(<parameters>) -> <return_type> @<mode> {
    <statements>
}
```

### 3.2 Key Keywords
- `manifest` - Function definition
- `create` - Object instantiation
- `crystal` - Universal return type
- `RADIANT_` - Prefix for luminous constructs
- `@ludicrous` - Performance mode annotation

### 3.3 Performance Modes
- `@standard` - Default execution
- `@ludicrous` - Maximum performance (3x speed)
- `@quantum` - Quantum computing preparation
- `@embedded` - Microcontroller optimization
- `@realtime` - Real-time guarantees

### 3.4 Type System
- **RADIANT** - String type (radiant = bright/clear text)
- **SHIMMER** - Number type (shimmer = fluid mathematics)
- **LUMINA** - Boolean type (lumina = light/dark)
- **CONSTELLATION** - Array type (ordered collection)
- **NEBULA** - Object/Map type (key-value cloud)
- **GALAXY** - Function type (executable system)
- **CRYSTAL** - Universal container type

---

## 4. Revolutionary Features

### 4.1 3D Emotion Synthesis
```lamia
create EMOTION_3D {
    primary: JOY,
    intensity: 0.8,
    spatial_coordinates: [x, y, z],
    duration: milliseconds
}
```

**Emotion Types:**
- JOY, SADNESS, ANGER, FEAR, SURPRISE, DISGUST
- Each with 3D spatial representation
- Intensity control (0.0-1.0)
- Duration-based decay

### 4.2 Social Protocols
```lamia
create SOCIAL_PROTOCOL {
    type: GREETING | FAREWELL | REQUEST | RESPONSE,
    culture: UNIVERSAL | FORMAL | CASUAL | INTIMATE,
    formality: CASUAL
}
```

**Protocol Support:**
- Media: `giphy://`, `ytube://`, `vimeo://`
- Social: `x://`, `insta://`, `tiktok://`, `discord://`
- Professional: `github://`, `linkedin://`, `slack://`
- E-commerce: `amazon://`, `shopify://`, `stripe://`

### 4.3 Native Manufacturing Integration
```lamia
create CNC_OPERATION {
    type: MILLING | DRILLING | TURNING,
    material: ALUMINUM | STEEL | PLASTIC,
    tool: T<number>,
    speed: RPM,
    feed: mm/min,
    gcode: NATIVE_GENERATION
}
```

**Manufacturing Features:**
- Direct G-code generation
- Arduino sketch transpilation
- CNC machine integration
- IoT device support

---

# PsiForceDB Licensing Server - Complete Deployment Guide

## 🎯 Overview

This guide will help you deploy the **PsiForceDB Licensing Server** with Discord and Patreon integration at:
- `https://licensing.psiforcedb.com`
- `https://licensing.lamia.website`

---

## 📋 Prerequisites

### Required Accounts:
1. **Discord Developer Account**
   - Bot Token with server permissions
   - Server ID where members join

2. **Patreon Creator Account**
   - Creator Access Token
   - Campaign ID
   - Tier IDs configured

3. **Domain & Hosting**
   - SSL certificate for HTTPS
   - Server with 2GB+ RAM

4. **GitHub Account** (for source code access)
   - Organization or personal account
   - Private repositories for source code

---

## 🔧 Step 1: Discord Bot Setup

### 1.1 Create Discord Bot
```
1. Go to https://discord.com/developers/applications
2. Click "New Application"
3. Name: "PsiForceDB License Bot"
4. Go to "Bot" section
5. Click "Add Bot"
6. Copy the BOT TOKEN (keep secret!)
7. Enable these Privileged Gateway Intents:
   - SERVER MEMBERS INTENT
   - MESSAGE CONTENT INTENT
```

### 1.2 Invite Bot to Server
```
1. Go to OAuth2 > URL Generator
2. Select scopes:
   - bot
   - applications.commands
3. Select permissions:
   - Read Messages/View Channels
   - Send Messages
   - Manage Roles
   - Read Message History
4. Copy generated URL and open in browser
5. Select your server and authorize
```

### 1.3 Get Server ID
```
1. Enable Developer Mode in Discord (Settings > Advanced > Developer Mode)
2. Right-click your server icon
3. Click "Copy ID"
4. This is your DISCORD_SERVER_ID
```

---

## 🎨 Step 2: Patreon API Setup

### 2.1 Create Patreon App
```
1. Go to https://www.patreon.com/portal/registration/register-clients
2. Click "Create Client"
3. Fill in details:
   - App Name: PsiForceDB Licensing
   - Description: License validation for supporters
   - Redirect URIs: https://licensing.psiforcedb.com/patreon/callback
4. Copy CLIENT_ID and CLIENT_SECRET
```

### 2.2 Get Creator Access Token
```
1. Go to https://www.patreon.com/portal/registration/register-clients
2. Click on your app
3. Copy "Creator's Access Token"
4. This is your PATREON_ACCESS_TOKEN
```

### 2.3 Get Campaign ID
```
1. Go to your Patreon page
2. URL format: https://www.patreon.com/YOUR_CAMPAIGN_NAME
3. Or use API: https://www.patreon.com/api/oauth2/v2/campaigns
4. Copy the campaign ID from response
```

### 2.4 Configure Tiers
```
Set up these tiers on Patreon:
- Basic: $1/month (not eligible for license)
- Supporter: $1+/month (ad-free license)
- Contributor: $5+/month (beta access)
- Champion: $10+/month (source code access)
- Enterprise: $100+/month (unlimited)
```

---

## ⚙️ Step 3: Server Configuration

### 3.1 Create Config File
Create `license_server_config.json`:
```json
{
  "database_path": "/var/lib/psiforcedb/licenses.db.json",
  "discord_bot_token": "YOUR_DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN_HERE",
  "patreon_access_token": "YOUR_PATREON_ACCESS_TOKEN_HERE",
  "discord_server_id": "YOUR_DISCORD_SERVER_ID",
  "patreon_campaign_id": "YOUR_PATREON_CAMPAIGN_ID",
  "minimum_patreon_cents": 100,
  "api_port": 8443,
  "use_ssl": true,
  "ssl_cert_path": "/etc/ssl/certs/psiforcedb.crt",
  "ssl_key_path": "/etc/ssl/private/psiforcedb.key",
  "log_level": "info",
  "sync_interval_minutes": 5,
  "github_org": "YOUR_GITHUB_ORG",
  "github_token": "YOUR_GITHUB_TOKEN"
}
```

### 3.2 Set Permissions
```bash
chmod 600 license_server_config.json
chown psiforcedb:psiforcedb license_server_config.json
```

---

## 🏗️ Step 4: Build & Deploy

### 4.1 Compile Server
```bash
cd /c/Build/lamia_clean_final

# Compile licensing server
g++ -std=c++17 -O3 \
    psiforce_license_server_main.cpp \
    psiforce_licensing_server.cpp \
    -o psiforce_license_server \
    -lcurl \
    -lssl -lcrypto \
    -lpthread \
    -I/usr/include/nlohmann \
    -static-libgcc -static-libstdc++
```

### 4.2 Deploy to Server
```bash
# Upload to server
scp psiforce_license_server root@licensing.psiforcedb.com:/usr/local/bin/
scp license_server_config.json root@licensing.psiforcedb.com:/etc/psiforcedb/

# Set permissions
ssh root@licensing.psiforcedb.com "chmod +x /usr/local/bin/psiforce_license_server"
```

### 4.3 Create Systemd Service
Create `/etc/systemd/system/psiforcedb-licensing.service`:
```ini
[Unit]
Description=PsiForceDB Licensing Server
After=network.target

[Service]
Type=simple
User=psiforcedb
Group=psiforcedb
WorkingDirectory=/var/lib/psiforcedb
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/psiforce_license_server /etc/psiforcedb/license_server_config.json
Restart=always
RestartSec=10
StandardOutput=journal
StandardError=journal

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
```

### 4.4 Start Service
```bash
systemctl daemon-reload
systemctl enable psiforcedb-licensing
systemctl start psiforcedb-licensing
systemctl status psiforcedb-licensing
```

---

## 🌐 Step 5: Web Portal Deployment

### 5.1 Deploy HTML Portal
```bash
# Upload to web server
scp licensing_web_portal.html root@licensing.psiforcedb.com:/var/www/licensing/index.html

# Update placeholders
ssh root@licensing.psiforcedb.com "
sed -i 's/YOUR_CAMPAIGN/YOUR_ACTUAL_CAMPAIGN_NAME/g' /var/www/licensing/index.html
sed -i 's/YOUR_INVITE/YOUR_DISCORD_INVITE_CODE/g' /var/www/licensing/index.html
sed -i 's/SUPPORTER_TIER_ID/YOUR_SUPPORTER_TIER_ID/g' /var/www/licensing/index.html
sed -i 's/CHAMPION_TIER_ID/YOUR_CHAMPION_TIER_ID/g' /var/www/licensing/index.html
"
```

### 5.2 Configure Nginx
Create `/etc/nginx/sites-available/licensing.psiforcedb.com`:
```nginx
server {
    listen 443 ssl http2;
    server_name licensing.psiforcedb.com licensing.lamia.website;

    ssl_certificate /etc/ssl/certs/psiforcedb.crt;
    ssl_certificate_key /etc/ssl/private/psiforcedb.key;

    root /var/www/licensing;
    index index.html;

    # API proxy to licensing server
    location /api/ {
        proxy_pass https://127.0.0.1:8443/;
        proxy_set_header Host $host;
        proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
    }

    # Static files
    location / {
        try_files $uri $uri/ =404;
    }

    # Security headers
    add_header X-Frame-Options "SAMEORIGIN" always;
    add_header X-Content-Type-Options "nosniff" always;
    add_header X-XSS-Protection "1; mode=block" always;
}

# Redirect HTTP to HTTPS
server {
    listen 80;
    server_name licensing.psiforcedb.com licensing.lamia.website;
    return 301 https://$host$request_uri;
}
```

Enable site:
```bash
ln -s /etc/nginx/sites-available/licensing.psiforcedb.com /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/
nginx -t
systemctl reload nginx
```

---

## 📊 Step 6: SEO Setup

### 6.1 Submit to Search Engines
```bash
# Google Search Console
https://search.google.com/search-console
- Add property: licensing.psiforcedb.com
- Verify ownership (DNS or HTML file)
- Submit sitemap: https://licensing.psiforcedb.com/sitemap.xml

# Bing Webmaster Tools
https://www.bing.com/webmasters
- Add site
- Verify
- Submit sitemap
```

### 6.2 Create Sitemap
Create `/var/www/licensing/sitemap.xml`:
```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<urlset xmlns="http://www.sitemaps.org/schemas/sitemap/0.9">
  <url>
    <loc>https://licensing.psiforcedb.com/</loc>
    <lastmod>2025-11-14</lastmod>
    <priority>1.0</priority>
  </url>
  <url>
    <loc>https://licensing.lamia.website/</loc>
    <lastmod>2025-11-14</lastmod>
    <priority>1.0</priority>
  </url>
</urlset>
```

### 6.3 Create robots.txt
Create `/var/www/licensing/robots.txt`:
```
User-agent: *
Allow: /
Sitemap: https://licensing.psiforcedb.com/sitemap.xml
```

---

## 🔐 Step 7: Security Hardening

### 7.1 SSL Certificate (Let's Encrypt)
```bash
certbot --nginx -d licensing.psiforcedb.com -d licensing.lamia.website
```

### 7.2 Firewall Rules
```bash
ufw allow 80/tcp
ufw allow 443/tcp
ufw allow 8443/tcp from 127.0.0.1  # Internal API only
ufw enable
```

### 7.3 Fail2Ban
```bash
# Install
apt install fail2ban

# Configure for nginx
cat > /etc/fail2ban/jail.local <<EOF
[nginx-http-auth]
enabled = true

[nginx-limit-req]
enabled = true
EOF

systemctl restart fail2ban
```

---

## 🧪 Step 8: Testing

### 8.1 Test Discord Integration
```bash
# Check if bot is online
curl https://licensing.psiforcedb.com/api/health

# Test user verification
curl -X POST https://licensing.psiforcedb.com/api/verify_discord \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"discord_id": "YOUR_DISCORD_ID"}'
```

### 8.2 Test Patreon Integration

```bash
    "discord_id": "YOUR_DISCORD_ID",

```

---

## 📈 Step 9: Monitoring

### 9.1 View Logs
```bash
# Server logs
journalctl -u psiforcedb-licensing -f

# Nginx logs
tail -f /var/log/nginx/access.log
tail -f /var/log/nginx/error.log
```

### 9.2 Check License Stats
```bash

# View stats
```

---

## 🎉 Step 10: Going Live!

### 10.1 Final Checklist
- [ ] Discord bot is online and responding
- [ ] Patreon integration verified
- [ ] SSL certificates valid
- [ ] Web portal loads correctly
- [ ] API endpoints working

```
Get your PsiForceDB & MedusaServ license today!
```
